items.q: Why do mature erythrocytes depend solely on the hexose monophosphate (HMP) shunt for maintaining reduced glutathione (GSH) reserves?
o: Red blood cells lack mitochondria and have no alternative pathway (e.g., malic enzyme or isocitrate DH) to generate NADPH
Erythrocytes synthesize glutathione only inside the nucleus
Glutathione reductase can use NADH in red cells but prefers NADPH
Glycolytic pyruvate kinase inhibits glutathione peroxidase
items.exp: Erythrocytes lack nuclei, ribosomes, and mitochondria. Because mitochondrial and cytoplasmic malic enzymes are absent, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) in the HMP shunt is the sole cellular source of NADPH required to reduce GSSG back to GSH.
r: Correct. Lacking mitochondria, red cells depend exclusively on G6PD for NADPH generation.
Incorrect. Red cells are anucleate.
Incorrect. Glutathione reductase has absolute specificity for NADPH.
Incorrect. Pyruvate kinase does not inhibit antioxidant enzymes.

items.q: A 24-year-old man takes primaquine before traveling to an endemic malaria zone. Three days later, he develops dark tea-colored urine, jaundice, and fatigue. Supravital staining of peripheral blood shows Heinz bodies. What do Heinz bodies consist of?
o: Precipitated aggregates of denatured hemoglobin crosslinked by disulfide bonds
Aggregates of ribosomal RNA and polyribosomes
items.exp: Under oxidative stress in G6PD-deficient erythrocytes, depleted reduced glutathione permits free radical oxidation of hemoglobin sulfhydryl groups. Denatured hemoglobin precipitates into Heinz bodies that adhere to red cell membranes.
r: Correct. Heinz bodies are insoluble precipitates of denatured, oxidized hemoglobin.
Incorrect. Ribosomal aggregates form basophilic stippling.
Incorrect. Nuclear chromatin remnants are Howell-Jolly bodies.
Incorrect. Iron granules form Pappenheimer bodies.

items.q: In G6PD deficiency, what mechanism produces the 'bite cells' (degmacytes) observed on peripheral blood smear during acute hemolytic crises?
o: Splenic macrophages pluck out membrane-bound Heinz bodies as erythrocytes traverse the cords of Billroth
Intravascular mechanical shearing by fibrin strands in microvilli
Autoimmune destruction by warm IgG antibodies
Spontaneous membrane vesiculation in hypertonic urine
items.exp: As erythrocytes squeeze through narrow interendothelial slits into splenic sinusoids, reticuloendothelial macrophages identify rigid Heinz bodies adhering to the membrane and excise them (pitting), creating bite cells (degmacytes).
r: Correct. Splenic macrophages excise Heinz bodies, leaving bite cells (degmacytes).
Incorrect. Fibrin shearing creates schistocytes in microangiopathies (TTP/HUS/DIC).
Incorrect. Warm autoimmune hemolysis produces spherocytes.
Incorrect. Urine tonicity does not create circulating bite cells.

items.q: Which enzyme in erythrocytes utilizes NADH to reduce methemoglobin (Fe3+) back to functional ferrous hemoglobin (Fe2+), maintaining normal methemoglobin below 1%?
items.exp: Cytochrome b5 reductase (diaphorase I) uses NADH generated by glycolysis to reduce cytochrome b5, which non-enzymatically reduces ferric iron (Fe3+) back to ferrous iron (Fe2+), maintaining normal methemoglobin <1%.
r: Correct. NADH-cytochrome b5 reductase is the primary physiological methemoglobin reductase.
Incorrect. G6PD generates NADPH, used by a secondary minor reductase pathway.
Incorrect. Glutathione peroxidase detoxifies peroxides.
Incorrect. Superoxide dismutase dismutates superoxide to H2O2.

items.q: Why can testing for erythrocyte G6PD enzyme activity immediately during an acute hemolytic crisis yield a falsely normal result?
o: The oldest G6PD-deficient erythrocytes have hemolyzed, leaving a reticulocyte-rich population with higher enzyme activity
Oxidative stress allosterically activates remaining mutant enzymes
Hemoglobinuria binds the assay reagent and gives artifactual color
Transfused platelets synthesize G6PD in the plasma sample
items.exp: Older red cells have the lowest G6PD activity and are selectively destroyed during acute hemolysis. The surviving marrow-released reticulocytes have high baseline G6PD activity, masking the underlying deficiency until 2-3 months later.
r: Correct. Older deficient cells hemolyze first; young reticulocytes have high enzyme levels, giving false-normal results.
Incorrect. Mutant enzymes are not allosterically activated by oxidants.
Incorrect. Assay interference is not the mechanism.
Incorrect. Platelets do not alter red cell lysate enzyme testing.

items.q: Which drug is well known for precipitating acute severe hemolytic crises in patients with G6PD deficiency?
items.exp: Rasburicase (recombinant urate oxidase) converts uric acid to allantoin and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). In G6PD deficiency, red cells cannot detoxify the massive H2O2 load, precipitating life-threatening hemolysis and methemoglobinemia.
r: Correct. Rasburicase generates H2O2 as a byproduct, triggering severe hemolysis in G6PD deficiency.
Incorrect. Penicillin causes drug-induced immune hemolytic anemia, not G6PD crisis.
Incorrect. Acetaminophen is safe at therapeutic doses.
Incorrect. Heparin does not induce oxidative stress.

items.q: In the Rapoport-Luebering glycolytic shunt, 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate is converted to 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate by bisphosphoglycerate mutase. What is the energetic sacrifice of this shunt?
o: Bypasses phosphoglycerate kinase, forfeiting 2 ATP molecules per glucose molecule
Consumes 2 additional ATP molecules per glucose
Prevents the reduction of NAD+ to NADH at GAPDH
Diverts pyruvate into the tricarboxylic acid cycle
items.exp: The Rapoport-Luebering shunt bypasses the phosphoglycerate kinase step. Normally, phosphoglycerate kinase produces 2 ATP (one per triose); by diverting through 2,3-BPG, red cells sacrifice these 2 ATP to regulate oxygen affinity.
r: Correct. Bypassing phosphoglycerate kinase yields zero net ATP for that glucose molecule.
Incorrect. It does not consume extra ATP.
Incorrect. GAPDH operates normally upstream.
Incorrect. Red cells lack mitochondria and cannot run the TCA cycle.

items.q: A 16-year-old boy presents with chronic mild jaundice, splenomegaly, and non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia. Direct Coombs test is negative. Erythrocyte 2,3-BPG levels are markedly elevated. Which enzymopathy is most likely?
items.exp: Pyruvate kinase deficiency is the most common glycolytic enzymopathy. Impaired conversion of PEP to pyruvate causes upstream accumulation of glycolytic intermediates, markedly elevating 2,3-BPG, which right-shifts the Hb curve and improves oxygen delivery.
r: Correct. Pyruvate kinase deficiency causes chronic hemolysis with characteristically elevated 2,3-BPG.
Incorrect. G6PD deficiency causes episodic hemolysis with normal 2,3-BPG.
Incorrect. GPI deficiency is far rarer and does not specifically elevate 2,3-BPG.
Incorrect. Glutathione synthetase deficiency impairs antioxidant defense.

items.q: What is the primary mode of inheritance for glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency?
items.exp: G6PD is encoded on the X chromosome (Xq28) and inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern. Hemizygous males manifest full disease; heterozygous females may be mildly symptomatic due to skewed lyonization (X-inactivation).
r: Correct. G6PD deficiency is an X-linked recessive disorder.
Incorrect. Pyruvate kinase deficiency is autosomal recessive.
Incorrect. Hereditary spherocytosis is mostly autosomal dominant.
Incorrect. Mitochondrial encephalomyopathies show maternal inheritance.
items.kp: G6PD deficiency is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern, predominantly affecting males while heterozygous females show variable expression due to lyonization.

items.q: Which antioxidant enzyme uses reduced glutathione (GSH) as a hydrogen donor to reduce dangerous hydrogen peroxide into harmless water?
items.exp: Glutathione peroxidase is a selenoprotein that converts H2O2 + 2 GSH into 2 H2O + GSSG. Glutathione reductase then uses NADPH to reduce GSSG back to 2 GSH.
r: Correct. Glutathione peroxidase oxidizes GSH to GSSG while reducing H2O2 to water.
Incorrect. Glutathione reductase regenerates GSH using NADPH.
Incorrect. Catalase dismutates H2O2 to water and O2 without using glutathione.
Incorrect. SOD converts superoxide to H2O2.
